text:
maria: heads-up — found a pathological case with encrypted safetensors + prefetch. when nodes prefetch 64 small shards concurrently we fire 64 KMS decrypts at once and blow the account quota. noticed in prod canary this morning.

ajay: ouch. is that 1 KMS call per shard or per file-open?

maria: per-shard header unwrap right now. we store per-shard wrapped DEK and call KMS:Decrypt to get the DEK, then decrypt locally. code path is in PrefetchWorker.handleShardOpen

lily: any short-term mitigations? rate limit KMS or backoff?

maria: rate limit helps but increases tail latency on hotstart. two options: 1) cache DEKs in RAM with a TTL (fast) 2) switch to a session key per model bundle — single KMS call for bundle, derive per-shard keys (needs manifest change)

zane: option 2 seems stronger long-term. less KMS pressure and fewer secrets in memory? though we need to think rotation and key compromise.

samir: can we do hybrid: bundle session key for hot path, fallback to per-shard wrapped DEK for cold loads? that lets us keep existing wrapped metadata for archival bundles.

maria: exactly my thinking. proposal: extend manifest header with optional field "enc_bundle_session": {"scheme":"kms-session-v1","wrap_alg":"AES-GCM","session_policy":"ephemeral"} when present, loader will attempt session unwrap first (single KMS call) and if it fails fallback to per-shard unwraps.

kevin: quick note on HSM: large customers want HSM-backed keys and deny session keys being cached on host. session approach might break that compliance surface. we need a guard to disable session path if owner's policy requires HSM-protected DEKs per-shard.

lily: ok add manifest flag "session_allowed": true/false. default false for Private deployments.

ajay: technical trade: session path reduces KMS QPS but adds a single point-of-failure. what about multi-tier fallback: session -> cached DEK -> per-shard unwrap?

maria: yes: loader tries in that order. also propose we cache derived per-shard DEKs for the life of the session key to avoid re-derive costs. eviction TTL should be model-bundle-scoped and bounded (e.g., 10m).

zane: we should quantify CPU cost of local AES-GCM decrypts on our warmup workers. on A100-ish hosts AES on CPU is cheap, but on smaller nodes it's non-trivial if we decrypt thousands of MB/s. maybe move decrypt to a lightweight enclave thread or use AES-NI path in Rust.

samir: another angle: can we decrypt and stream shards directly into GPU memory, bypassing host RAM? saves copy but complicates integrity checks.

maria: risky. streaming-to-GPU is nice for perf but if a shard fails integrity mid-stream we need a rollback path. also makes prefetch cache eviction more painful.

kevin: operational question: if session unwrap fails because KMS rate limit triggered, we should avoid thundering herd re-tries. we need jittered backoff and a global coordinator per node to serialize head-of-line session unwrapping for a bundle.

lily: propose PrefetchCoordinator with per-bundle in-flight semaphore. first prefetcher does session unwrap, others await the result (with timeout). simplifies rate pattern.

ajay: +1. add metrics: kms.session_unwrap_latency, kms.session_unwrap_errors, kms.per_shard_unwrap_count.

zane: manifest schema snippet for proposal (pseudo):

```
{"manifest_version":2,
 "model_name":"llama-x",
 "shards":[{"path":"s1.safetensors","wrap":"wrapped_dek_v1"},...],
 "encryption":{
   "session_allowed":true,
   "session_hint":"kms-session-v1",
   "per_shard_wrap":"wrapped_dek_v1"
 }
}
```

samir: we should also embed an "enc_priority_hint" per shard for warmup ordering — small attention layers first, large vocab tables later. encrypted blobs could carry higher priority to ensure session unwrap benefits hot prefixes.

maria: agreed. add field "warmup_priority": int where lower is higher priority. loader sorts prefetch queue by (session_available, warmup_priority, shard_size) to maximize warm path benefits.

kevin: customer privacy: what about edge case where session_allowed true but customer's audit requires per-shard per-request logging in KMS? we need an allowlist of customers that can use session path. control plane should inject session_allowed at bundle registration time.

lily: will coordinate with product and compliance to default to false for enterprise until we have attestation docs.

ajay: fallbacks for cold start: if both session and per-shard unwrap fail, we should surface a graceful degrade to read-only mode with smaller model variant (un-encrypted) if the policy allows, else fail-fast. policy-driven fallback.

maria: implement policy enum: {STRICT, ALLOW_UNENCRYPTED_FALLBACK, ALLOW_SMALLER_MODEL_FALLBACK}. default STRICT for private clusters.

zane: one more: instrument prefetch decision tree so we can A/B test session vs per-shard in staging. add experiment flag: EXP_SESSION_PREFETCH=true.

samir: test plan: 1) canary with synthetic load exercising 200 concurrent prefetche requests 2) measure KMS QPS, burst errors, warmup latency p95 3) measure memory and CPU decrypt throughput 4) validate manifest rotation/rollout semantics

maria: i'll draft a short RFC patch to manifest v2 with fields: encryption.session_allowed, encryption.session_hint, shards[*].warmup_priority, and loader behavior. will include coordinator pseudocode and metrics.

infra-bot: deploy queued: rolling canary to prefetchnode pool scheduled at 2024-11-02T14:10:00Z (dry-run) :robot_face:

lily: thanks all. ping me when draft is ready, i'll sync with compliance/product before we enable session_allowed in the registry.

maria: thanks — will post RFC link here when ready.
